sentences.cn_text: 1869年12月，国会任命了一个委员会，负责选址并为新国务院大楼编制设计方案和成本预算。
sentences.en_text: In December of 1869, Congress appointed a commission to select a site and prepare plans and cost estimates for a new State Department Building.

sentences.cn_text: 该委员会还需考虑战争部和海军部的可能布局安排。
sentences.en_text: The commission was also to consider possible arrangements for the War and Navy Departments.

sentences.cn_text: 一些人原本期待在白宫另一侧建造一座希腊复兴风格的财政部姊妹楼，但最终采用的是阿尔弗雷德·穆莱特设计的华丽法国第二帝国风格方案，令他们大感意外。1871年6月，一座容纳三个部门的大楼开始动工。
sentences.en_text: To the horror of some who expected a Greek Revival twin of the Treasury Building to be erected on the other side of the White House, the elaborate French Second Empire style design by Alfred Mullett was selected, and construction of a building to house all three departments began in June of 1871.

sentences.cn_text: 国务院南翼于1875年竣工，是最先启用的部分，内有精美的四层图书馆（1876年竣工）、外交接待室，以及装饰有雕花木饰、东方地毯和模版墙面图案的部长办公室。
sentences.en_text: Completed in 1875, the State Department’s south wing was the first to be occupied, with its elegant four-story library (completed in 1876), Diplomatic Reception Room, and Secretary’s office decorated with carved wood, oriental rugs, and stenciled wall patterns.

sentences.cn_text: 海军部于1879年迁入东翼，部长办公室装饰有精细的墙面和天花板模版图案以及镶木拼花地板。
sentences.en_text: The Navy Department moved into the east wing in 1879, where elaborate wall and ceiling stenciling and marquetry floors decorated the office of the Secretary.

sentences.cn_text: 国务、战争与海军大楼（其原名）容纳了三个行政部门，这些部门在19世纪最后25年和20世纪前25年期间与制定和执行国家外交政策关系最为密切——这正是美国崛起为国际强国的时期。
sentences.en_text: The State, War, and Navy Building, as it was originally known, housed the three Executive Branch Departments most intimately associated with formulating and conducting the nation’s foreign policy in the last quarter of the nineteenth century and the first quarter of the twentieth century — the period when the United States emerged as an international power.

sentences.cn_text: 该建筑曾接纳过国家一些最重要的外交官和政治家，并见证了诸多历史事件。
sentences.en_text: The building has housed some of the nation’s most significant diplomats and politicians and has been the scene of many historic events.

sentences.cn_text: 许多最负盛名的国家人物都曾参与在EEOB花岗岩墙内发生的历史事件。
sentences.en_text: Many of the most celebrated national figures have participated in historical events that have taken place within the EEOB’s granite walls.

sentences.cn_text: 西奥多·罗斯福、富兰克林·D·罗斯福、威廉·霍华德·塔夫脱、德怀特·D·艾森豪威尔、林登·B·约翰逊、杰拉尔德·福特和乔治·H·W·布什在成为总统之前，都曾在这座建筑内设有办公室。
sentences.en_text: Theodore and Franklin D. Roosevelt, William Howard Taft, Dwight D. Eisenhower, Lyndon B. Johnson, Gerald Ford, and George H. W. Bush all had offices in this building before becoming President.

sentences.cn_text: 它曾容纳过16位海军部长、21位战争部长和24位国务卿。
sentences.en_text: It has housed 16 Secretaries of the Navy, 21 Secretaries of War, and 24 Secretaries of State.

sentences.cn_text: 温斯顿·丘吉尔曾在其走廊中漫步，珍珠港事件后日本使节也曾在此与国务卿科德尔·赫尔会晤。
sentences.en_text: Winston Churchill once walked its corridors and Japanese emissaries met here with Secretary of State Cordell Hull after the bombing of Pearl Harbor.

sentences.cn_text: 艾森豪威尔行政办公楼（EEOB）在美国国家历史和建筑遗产中占据着独特地位。
sentences.en_text: The Eisenhower Executive Office Building (EEOB) commands a unique position in both the national history and the architectural heritage of the United States.

tokens.gloss: 艾森豪威尔行政办公楼

sentences.cn_text: 它由财政部监理建筑师阿尔弗雷德·B·穆莱特设计，于1871年至1888年间建造，用于容纳不断扩充的国务院、战争部和海军部工作人员，被视为美国法国第二帝国建筑风格的典范之一。
sentences.en_text: Designed by Supervising Architect of the Treasury, Alfred B. Mullett, it was built from 1871 to 1888 to house the growing staffs of the State, War, and Navy Departments, and is considered one of the best examples of French Second Empire architecture in the country.

sentences.cn_text: 建造历时17年，大楼逐翼逐翼缓慢升起。
sentences.en_text: Construction took 17 years as the building slowly rose wing by wing.

sentences.cn_text: EEOB建成时是华盛顿最大的办公楼，拥有近两英里长的黑白瓷砖走廊。
sentences.en_text: When the EEOB was finished, it was the largest office building in Washington, with nearly 2 miles of black and white tiled corridors.

sentences.cn_text: 几乎所有内部装饰均采用铸铁或石膏制作；木材用量被降至最低以确保防火安全。
sentences.en_text: Almost all of the interior detail is of cast iron or plaster; the use of wood was minimized to insure fire safety.

sentences.cn_text: 八座宏伟的花岗岩弧形楼梯配有超过4000根单独铸造的青铜栏杆，顶部由四个天窗圆顶和两个彩色玻璃圆厅覆盖。
sentences.en_text: Eight monumental curving staircases of granite with over 4,000 individually cast bronze balusters are capped by four skylight domes and two stained glass rotundas.

sentences.cn_text: EEOB的历史早在其地基奠定之前便已开始。
sentences.en_text: The history of the EEOB began long before its foundations were laid.

sentences.cn_text: 最早的行政办公楼建于1799年至1820年间。
sentences.en_text: The first executive offices were constructed between 1799 and 1820.

sentences.cn_text: 一系列火灾（包括1814年英军纵火）以及过度拥挤的状况促使现有财政部大楼的修建。
sentences.en_text: A series of fires (including those set by the British in 1814) and overcrowded conditions led to the construction of the existing Treasury Building.

sentences.cn_text: 1866年，财政部大楼北翼的施工需要拆除国务院大楼。
sentences.en_text: In 1866, the construction of the North Wing of the Treasury Building necessitated the demolition of the State Department building.
